description: Given Dagster run-status sensors, sensor factories, or op hooks that send notifications, author the matching Orchestra alerts: block — pipeline-level for job-scoped sensors, task-level for op-scoped hooks — with the correct required field per destination type (destination for SLACK/EMAIL, connection_id for PAGER_DUTY/TEAMS/WEBHOOK/DATADOG).

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster run-failure sensor to an Orchestra pipeline-level alert (see files/run_failure_sensor_multi.py). It pages PagerDuty and also posts to the #incidents Slack channel on failure. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live paging, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A pipeline-level alerts: entry firing on FAILED with two destinations: PAGER_DUTY (connection_id set, no destination field) and SLACK (destination: '#incidents', no connection_id field).

assertions.text: The PAGER_DUTY destination sets connection_id (SLACK/EMAIL require destination; PAGER_DUTY/TEAMS/WEBHOOK/DATADOG require connection_id)
A SLACK destination targeting #incidents is present

evals.prompt: Convert these Dagster failure notifications to Orchestra pipeline-level alerts (see files/email_and_teams_sensors.py) — both the email sensor and the Microsoft Teams webhook it mentions. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A pipeline-level alerts: entry (or entries) firing on FAILED with an EMAIL destination (destination: 'data-team@example.com') and a MICROSOFT_TEAMS destination (connection_id: teams_webhook_54321).

assertions.text: The EMAIL destination sets destination (SLACK/EMAIL require destination, not connection_id)
data-team@example.com is carried over as the EMAIL destination value
teams_webhook_54321 is carried over as the MICROSOFT_TEAMS connection_id

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster op-level failure hook to an Orchestra task-level alert on the critical_transform task only — it should not fire for the whole pipeline (see files/failure_hook_task_level.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live events, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A task-level alerts: entry on the critical-transform task (not the pipeline root) firing on FAILED with a DATADOG destination (connection_id set, parameters.priority present), since op-scoped hooks map to task-level alerts, not job-wide sensors.

assertions.text: The DATADOG destination sets a parameters.priority value
The alert is placed on the critical-transform TaskModel (task-level), not the pipeline root alerts: block — matching the op-scoped @failure_hook rather than a job-wide run-status sensor
downstream_report, which has no hook, does not also get this alert
The DATADOG connection_id follows the name_XXXXX suffix convention (a plausible placeholder) rather than being left as a bare invented name, or is flagged as needing a real value from the user
